classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate inverse trigonometric composites and use point coordinates and perpendicular gradients to find two line equations.

content.prompt: Find, in the form $y=mx+b$, the equation of the tangent and the normal to each curve at the point indicated:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{6}{\sqrt{1-9x^2}}.\end{aligned}$$
At $x=0$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}&=-6,\\y&=2\cos^{-1}(0)\\&=\pi.\end{aligned}$$
The normal gradient is $-\frac{1}{(-6)}=\frac16$.

Tangent:
$$\begin{aligned}y-\pi&=-6(x-0),\\y&=-6x+\pi.\end{aligned}$$
Normal:
$$\begin{aligned}y-\pi&=\frac16(x-0),\\y&=\frac{x}{6}+\pi.\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{\frac12}{\sqrt{1-\frac{x^2}{4}}}\\&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}.\end{aligned}$$
At $x=\sqrt2$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\\y&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)\\&=\frac{\pi}{4}.\end{aligned}$$
The normal gradient is $-\sqrt2$.

Tangent:
$$\begin{aligned}y-\frac{\pi}{4}&=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}(x-\sqrt2),\\y&=\frac{x}{\sqrt2}+\frac{\pi}{4}-1.\end{aligned}$$
Normal:
$$\begin{aligned}y-\frac{\pi}{4}&=-\sqrt2(x-\sqrt2),\\y&=-\sqrt2x+\frac{\pi}{4}+2.\end{aligned}$$
